verdicts.misleading_risk: Medium. (1) Funding: the preprint's Acknowledgements paragraph is long, has per-person attributions ('to G.J.', 'to R.H.'), grant numbers and a mandatory EU disclaimer, and contains an apparent typo ('and 35791' in the InFLAMES decision numbers; checked in the arXiv v1 PDF text). Copying it verbatim reproduces the typo, and a partial copy drops the attributions and disclaimer, so a visitor could read it as 'these funders fund this site or the app catalogue'. (2) Affiliations are March 2026 (v1). The Zenodo record (0.0.2, 2026-06-19) lists different affiliations for Hidalgo-Cenalmor (Instituto Gulbenkian de Ciencia), Rivera Pineda (Euro-BioImaging ERIC) and Saraiva (Molecular Structural and Cellular Microbiology), so a page that shows the preprint's institutions as people's institutions may already be stale. It must say 'as printed in the preprint, v1'. (3) Listing five named people on a public site needs their agreement. (4) The page must not use the preprint contribution paragraph or imply who built the site.
verdicts.refined_proposal:
Build a much smaller page. No new generator, no YAML, no new test module, no llms.py line. Hand-write content/credits.md, the way content/submit.md is done (already listed under 'Hand-written here'), and publish it with a short page_credits next to page_submit in pages_site.py, with menu="ecosystem/" (or whatever the owner chooses) and an edit link to content/credits.md. Add one DESIGN.md line saying the page is plain prose with h2 sections. Content, all of it checkable against the arXiv v1 PDF I read:
- h1 'People and credits'.
- One lead paragraph: LabConstrictor is described in the preprint 'Packaging Jupyter notebooks as installable desktop apps using LabConstrictor' (arXiv:2603.10704, v1, 11 March 2026) by Iván Hidalgo-Cenalmor, Marcela Xiomara Rivera Pineda, Bruno M. Saraiva, Ricardo Henriques and Guillaume Jacquemet. Link to https://arxiv.org/abs/2603.10704.
- The six affiliations exactly as printed and numbered, and the five author lines with the printed numbers (1,2 / 1,2,3 / 4 / 4,5 / 1,2,3,6). The PDF confirms this mapping. Introduce them with 'Affiliations as printed in the preprint (March 2026); they may have changed since.' Correspondence: G. Jacquemet.
- Funding: one sentence, 'Funding is listed in the Acknowledgements of the preprint', with the arXiv link. Only add funder names or grant numbers if an author supplies and approves the text; in that case copy it whole, including the 'to X' attributions and the EU disclaimer, and have the authors check the typo.
- No contribution paragraph, no ORCIDs, no logos, no artwork credit (authorship of the logo and comic is unknown).
Author decisions needed before it ships: consent of the five listed people, and whether to show the March 2026 or current affiliations. Never write a person's name here as a credit beyond the preprint's own author list. The citation block belongs to the citation dimension; link to it, do not duplicate it.
verdicts.evidence: Verified: 0 of 38 pages mention authors, arXiv, preprint or funding (grep of site/). Footer line at overrides/main.html:102. arXiv abs page confirms title, five authors in that order, v1, 11 Mar 2026. The v1 PDF (pdftotext) confirms the six affiliation lines, the author numbering 1,2 / 1,2,3 / 4 / 4,5 / 1,2,3,6, 'Correspondence: (G. Jacquemet)', the contribution paragraph naming only G.J., I.H.-C. and M.R., and the funding paragraph with the typo. The preprint text never contains 'Cell Migration Lab'. The Zenodo API shows the creators' affiliations differ from the preprint. scripts/lcsite/pages_site.py is 101 lines and has page_submit reading content/submit.md, which is the cheap precedent. AGENTS.md already lists content/ files as hand-written. check_site requires one current top-menu entry, so menu= is needed as proposed.

verdicts.misleading_risk: Medium for the proposed wording. 'A project of the Cell Migration Lab (Abo Akademi University and Turku Bioscience Centre), with co-authors at ITQB NOVA and UCL' puts universities' names in a footer, which reads as institutional backing nobody has agreed to. 'co-authors' of the project are really co-authors of the preprint, and 'ITQB NOVA' and 'UCL' are short forms, not the printed affiliation texts ('Instituto de Tecnologia Quimica e Biologica Antonio Xavier, Universidade Nova de Lisboa'; 'UCL Laboratory for Molecular Cell Biology'). The Zenodo record gives different affiliations for several authors, so a footer claim is the least safe place for them. The current 'A project of the Cell Migration Lab' is supported by the template LICENSE ('Copyright (c) 2025 Cell Migration Lab') and the GitHub organisation. The auditor's claim of a '(c) Cell Migration Lab' footer is wrong: the built site contains 0 '(c)' characters.
verdicts.refined_proposal: Keep the footer sentence as it is. Add only one <li> to the footer's second list (or one text link after the sentence): 'People and credits' -> credits/ (internal, same tab), once G1's page exists. No institutions, no 'co-authors', no copyright line. Dead data cleanup: delete data/site.yaml `org`, `org_url` and `links.citation_doi` only after checking nothing reads them (my grep of scripts, overrides and tests finds no reader). The footer DOI at main.html:100 is hard-coded, and which DOI it should be is for the citation dimension to decide. Do NOT remove mkdocs.yml `site_author`: it is rendered as <meta name="author"> in every page. `copyright:` in mkdocs.yml is not rendered anywhere (0 occurrences of the © sign in site/index.html); either delete it or leave it. It is harmless, so low priority. A tidy-up, not a major gap.
verdicts.evidence: overrides/main.html:102 and :100. LICENSE line 3 of /home/user/LabConstrictor says 'Copyright (c) 2025 Cell Migration Lab'. grep of site/index.html: <meta name="author" content="Cell Migration Lab"> present, 0 '(c)' signs. grep finds no code reading `org`, `org_url` or `citation_doi` in scripts/, overrides/ or tests/. /home/user/website/mkdocs.yml line 10 describes the lab as 'Abo Akademi University and Turku Bioscience Centre'. The preprint PDF never mentions 'Cell Migration Lab'.

verdicts.misleading_risk: Low for the gap as a concern, but the proposed machinery adds risk. A build that parses the template README and an arXiv API check would fail the live daily build on harmless rewording, or on a v2 that changes nothing about the credits. Also the 'checked_on' line ('Checked against the preprint on <date>') asserts a verification that a human must really have done; an automatic date would overstate it. The claim that the Zenodo record disagrees for '4 of 5' authors is loose: Hidalgo-Cenalmor, Rivera Pineda and Saraiva clearly differ. Henriques ('Universidade Nova de Lisboa') and Jacquemet ('Abo Akademi University') are consistent subsets of the preprint's affiliations.
verdicts.refined_proposal: Drop G3 as a code feature. With the slim G1 (names and printed affiliations in one hand-written file, funding by link only) there is nothing to drift: the preprint reference stays in the template README, the site's credits file is the only copy of the affiliations, and Zenodo is archive metadata. Do two cheap things. (a) Add one line to AGENTS.md 'Sources of truth': 'People page: content/credits.md, copied from the preprint (arXiv v1); the template README Citation holds the reference; the Zenodo record is not a source.' (b) Put the preprint version and the date a person last compared the file with the preprint in a visible sentence on the page, entered by hand. Tell the Zenodo record owners (the authors) that their creator affiliations differ from the preprint, for the .zenodo.json fix, but make no site change. Leave the template README line (a link to the site's credits page) as an optional pull request for the owners. A build-time README check and an arXiv metadata check are not worth their cost for a six-app site and would break the 'build never blocks on cosmetic text' goal.
verdicts.evidence: AGENTS.md line 28 says the template's card is inline because the repo is copied into every app, which supports keeping funding text out of the template. The template README Citation section (lines 66-69 of /home/user/LabConstrictor/README.md) already holds the five names in the preprint's order and the arXiv DOI 10.48550/arXiv.2603.10704. Zenodo API for record 20758747: title LabConstrictor, version 0.0.2, publication date 2026-06-19, 5 creators in the same order, affiliations 'Instituto Gulbenkian de Ciencia', 'Euro-BioImaging ERIC', 'Molecular Structural and Cellular Microbiology', 'Universidade Nova de Lisboa', 'Abo Akademi University', and a related identifier 'describes arXiv:2603.10704'. grep finds no reader of citation_doi.

verdicts.misleading_risk: Low if left to the app owners; real risk if the site invents attribution. Never write app authors on the site, only in each app's manifest. VLab4Mic is the sensitive case: it is a Henriques-lab tool published through a CellMigrationLab fork, it is `featured: true`, and its page lists no author or origin. The manifest description does say 'desktop installer distribution of VLab4Mic', but not whose or that it is a fork. Do not guess who authored the fork's installers or whether the Henriques lab agreed.
verdicts.refined_proposal: Keep the site untouched; this is an issue or message to the app owners, not a site PR. (1) Each of NucleiSky, CellTracksColab, GuessTheCondition, Playground, Demo and VLab4Mic adds `authors:` (name, optional orcid) to its own labconstrictor-app.yaml, copied by the owners from the app's own reference (NucleiSky README BibTeX lists 8 authors; CellTracksColab README lists 7). pages_apps.details_list already prints the row (line 148) and escapes the names. (2) For VLab4Mic, ask the owners to choose between (a) pointing the registry entry at HenriquesLab/LabConstrictor-VLab4Mic once the manifest and installers exist there, and (b) keeping the fork and stating its origin in the manifest `description` plus `authors`. Option (a) means re-adding the registry entry with a new repo_id, owner_id and a maintainer re-check, since the registry pauses a listing when the owner changes. Until they decide, consider asking the maintainers whether `featured: true` should stay. Only say it is a fork if the owners confirm the wording. Everything else is out of scope for this dimension.
